ICT Academy

76 concept records across seven learning tracks from the supplied ICT Futures playbook. Concepts include evidence/provenance notes; an educator search link is not represented as a verified lesson video.

Market Structure

Market Structure

Framework for reading swing highs, swing lows and directional sequences. The playbook uses higher-timeframe structure for context before lower-timeframe execution.

Open module →BeginnerMarket Structure

Swing High & Swing Low

Local turning points used to map structure. The exact pivot lookback is a rule that must be fixed.

Open module →BeginnerMarket Structure

Break of Structure (BOS)

A break of a prior structural swing in the direction of the existing trend. It is a continuation clue, not an automatic entry.

Open module →BeginnerMarket Structure

Market Structure Shift (MSS)

A break through a relevant swing opposite to prior short-term structure, ideally with displacement. In the playbook, MSS confirms after a liquidity raid.

Open module →IntermediateMarket Structure

CHoCH terminology comparison

Change of Character is used by parts of the wider price-action/SMC community. The supplied playbook prefers MSS for its reversal framework.

Open module →IntermediateMarket Structure

Displacement

A fast directional move with relatively large candle bodies that breaks a meaningful swing and may leave imbalances. The PDF says the threshold is discretionary.

Open module →IntermediateLiquidity

Liquidity

In ICT terminology, liquidity refers to orders or stops thought to cluster around obvious highs, lows and reference levels. The playbook uses pools to frame draw on liquidity.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Buy-Side Liquidity (BSL)

A label for potential buy stops and breakout orders above visible highs. The playbook places BSL above equal highs and prior/session highs.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Sell-Side Liquidity (SSL)

A label for potential sell stops and breakout orders below visible lows; counterpart to BSL.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Equal Highs (EQH)

Two or more swing highs at approximately similar prices. The area above them is considered potential BSL.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Equal Lows (EQL)

Two or more swing lows at approximately similar prices. The area below them is considered potential SSL.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Prior Day High / Low (PDH / PDL)

Previous trading day high and low. The playbook treats these as important intraday liquidity references and frequent objectives.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Prior Week High / Low (PWH / PWL)

Previous completed week high and low; higher-timeframe liquidity reference levels.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Session High / Low

High and low formed during a defined session, such as Asia or London. The PDF uses these as potential sweep levels.

Open module →BeginnerLiquidity

Liquidity Sweep / Raid

Price trades beyond an obvious liquidity level and closes back inside under the playbook's simplified description. A sweep alone is not an entry.

Open module →IntermediateLiquidity

Liquidity Run / Breakout Acceptance

A move through a liquidity level that continues instead of rejecting back inside. The playbook distinguishes a run from a sweep.

Open module →IntermediateLiquidity

Internal & External Range Liquidity (IRL / ERL)

External liquidity refers to highs/lows outside a dealing range; internal references include imbalances/zones inside it. Movement between them is a conceptual model.

Open module →AdvancedLiquidity

Opposing Liquidity / Draw on Liquidity

The next relevant liquidity pool in the direction of a directional hypothesis. The PDF's models often target opposing liquidity after entry.

Open module →IntermediateImbalances

Fair Value Gap (FVG)

Three-candle price imbalance. Bullish: candle 3 low is above candle 1 high. Bearish: candle 3 high is below candle 1 low. It is an entry zone in some models, not a signal by itself.

Open module →IntermediateImbalances

Higher-Timeframe FVG

An FVG on a larger timeframe such as 1H, 4H or Daily, used as context on a lower execution timeframe.

Open module →IntermediateImbalances

Consequent Encroachment (CE)

The 50% midpoint of an FVG. Some practitioners treat touch of this midpoint as partial mitigation or entry reference.

Open module →IntermediateImbalances

Inversion Fair Value Gap (IFVG)

A gap whose role is treated as reversed after price closes through its far edge. The playbook specifies a body close, not merely a wick.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances

Balanced Price Range (BPR)

Overlap between a bullish FVG and a bearish FVG. The PDF describes it as a consolidation/reference zone, not inherently directional.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances

Volume Imbalance

A gap between consecutive candle bodies while their wicks overlap. It is distinct from the three-candle FVG definition.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances

First Presented FVG (FPFVG)

The first FVG of a session that meets trader-defined qualification rules. The PDF labels its perceived quality a community convention.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances

Liquidity Void

A fast one-sided move leaving relatively little two-way trading or overlapping candles. The PDF lists liquidity voids among PD Array references.

Open module →AdvancedBlocks & PD Arrays

Order Block (OB)

Last opposing candle/zone before a displacement move. The PDF stresses that displacement quality makes the zone meaningful.

Open module →IntermediateBlocks & PD Arrays

Mean Threshold (MT)

The 50% level of an Order Block range. Different practitioners may define the OB boundary differently.

Open module →IntermediateBlocks & PD Arrays

Breaker Block

A failed Order Block whose polarity is treated as reversed after price closes through it. A return may be studied as a pullback.

Open module →AdvancedBlocks & PD Arrays

Mitigation Block

The PDF distinguishes a mitigation block from a breaker, describing a zone associated with mitigation in a reversal structure; definitions vary.

Open module →AdvancedBlocks & PD Arrays

Rejection Block

A zone around a rejection from a reference extreme. Definitions vary, so the page treats it as a glossary topic requiring a fixed rule.

Open module →AdvancedEntry Models

Unicorn Model

The PDF defines Unicorn as overlap between a Breaker Block and an FVG, usually after a sweep and shift.

Open module →AdvancedBlocks & PD Arrays

PD Arrays

Umbrella term for old highs/lows, OBs, FVGs, liquidity voids, breakers, mitigation and rejection blocks.

Open module →IntermediateRange & Retracement

Premium & Discount

Within a defined dealing range, above the 50% equilibrium is premium and below is discount. The PDF advises using a range formed by a meaningful structural event.

Open module →BeginnerRange & Retracement

Equilibrium (EQ)

The 50% midpoint of a defined dealing range; it separates premium from discount.

Open module →BeginnerRange & Retracement

Dealing Range

A high-to-low range chosen from a meaningful structural event, such as BOS or MSS; basis for premium/discount analysis.

Open module →IntermediateRange & Retracement

Optimal Trade Entry (OTE)

The PDF describes a retracement band around 62%–79% of an impulsive leg, with 70.5% as a midpoint convention.

Open module →IntermediateRange & Retracement

Fibonacci / Range Extensions

Extensions such as -27% and -62% are cited as potential measured objectives. Their use is convention and depends on anchors.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Sessions

Time Anchors

The PDF lists Midnight/True Day Open, 08:30 ET data reference, 09:30 ET cash open, NDOG and NWOG.

Open module →IntermediateTime & Sessions

Midnight / True Day Open

00:00 New York price used by the playbook as a daily reference, not necessarily broker server midnight or exchange day open.

Open module →IntermediateTime & Sessions

New Day Opening Gap (NDOG)

Gap between previous day's close and new day's opening reference under a chosen ICT convention. The PDF distinguishes NDOG from an ordinary FVG.

Open module →IntermediateTime & Sessions

New Week Opening Gap (NWOG)

Gap between prior week's close and new week's open. The PDF treats it as a support/resistance or magnet hypothesis.

Open module →IntermediateTime & Sessions

Weekly Open

Opening reference for the new futures trading week, often near Sunday Globex reopen for CME products. Schedules vary by product/holiday.

Open module →IntermediateTime & Sessions

ICT Killzones

Time windows to pay attention to potential setups. The PDF includes Forex and index-specific windows. A killzone tells when, not where or direction.

Open module →BeginnerTime & Sessions

Asian Range

The PDF's reference range is 20:00–00:00 New York time. Its high/low become potential liquidity references for London/NY.

Open module →BeginnerTime & Sessions

Silver Bullet

Three one-hour New York windows in the PDF: 03:00–04:00, 10:00–11:00 and 14:00–15:00 ET. Entry requires an FVG formed inside the selected window.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Narrative

AMD / Power of Three

Accumulation, Manipulation and Distribution as a daily narrative. The PDF associates accumulation with Asia, manipulation with London/NY and later distribution.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Narrative

Judas Swing

Session-associated false push through a marked level, often around London/NY opens, followed by a move the other way. The PDF says to use pre-defined daily bias.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Narrative

IPDA 20/40/60 Lookback

The PDF frames 20-, 40- and 60-trading-day highs/lows as reference ranges. It says algorithm language is a model, not a proven mechanism.

Open module →AdvancedCross-Market

SMT Divergence

Related markets fail to confirm comparable highs/lows around the same time. PDF pairs include NQ/ES/YM, 6E/6B/DX and GC/SI.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Narrative

ICT Weekly Profiles

Possible Tuesday/Wednesday weekly-high/low and midweek-reversal tendencies. PDF labels them tendencies, not fixed rules.

Open module →AdvancedCross-Market

Index SMT: NQ / ES / YM / RTY

The playbook compares NQ, ES and YM for non-confirming highs/lows; RTY adds small-cap/risk-appetite context.

Open module →AdvancedCross-Market

FX & Metals SMT Pairs

The PDF describes 6E/6B versus DX (inverse comparison) and GC versus SI. Swings should match in time and expiry when applicable.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Sessions

Central Bank Dealers Range (CBDR)

PDF describes CBDR around 14:00–20:00 ET, often using candle bodies in some sources; source variation noted.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Sessions

Flout Range

Extended CBDR-style range. PDF notes sources differ on exact start (14:00 or 15:00 ET) through midnight.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Sessions

Standard-Deviation Projections

The PDF repeats an anchor range height as a projection unit at ±1, ±2 and ±2.5. It explicitly says this is not statistical standard deviation.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Narrative

ICT Macros — Research Note

The PDF deliberately omits a fixed ICT Macros list because sources disagree on exact time segments. This page documents uncertainty rather than inventing a canonical list.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Sessions

Midnight Open vs Exchange Trading-Day Open

ICT midnight open is a New York reference. It is not necessarily the exchange trading-day open or broker server-day open.

Open module →IntermediateMarket Structure

Change in State of Delivery (CISD)

A short-term delivery-change label used when price closes through a chosen opening-price reference from a prior directional candle run. It is a defined close/open observation, not proof of institutional intent.

Open module →IntermediateDaily Narrative

Market Maker Model (MMXM)

A broad campaign narrative describing price moving away from an origin range in stages, reaching a higher-timeframe reference area, and potentially reversing through prior ranges or pauses. The wording does not prove the actual orders or intentions of a market maker.

Open module →AdvancedLiquidity

Turtle Soup (false-breakout setup)

A false breakout of a prior high or low that fails and reverses back through the level. The label originated outside ICT and is also used in later SMC/ICT discussions.

Open module →IntermediatePD Arrays

Propulsion Block

A specialised order-block refinement described in some ICT education. Secondary definitions describe an order-block reaction and a subsequent close through a reference candle level, but the exact sequence differs by source.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances & Gaps

Breakaway Gap

A label found in some secondary ICT/SMC references for an imbalance left behind during a decisive move that does not promptly rebalance. It should not be confused with an exchange-session opening gap.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Session Concepts

Opening Range Gap (ORG)

A session-reference gap label appearing in some ICT transcript indexes. The exact opening session and price anchors are not universally specified, so they must be documented from the source being followed.

Open module →AdvancedImbalances & Gaps

Event Horizon (EH)

A niche term in some transcript-indexed ICT glossaries for a midpoint reference derived between two opening-gap structures, such as NDOG and NWOG. It is not a core, universal ICT definition.

Open module →AdvancedPD Arrays

Reclaimed Order Block

A community label for a previously violated or lost order-block area that price later re-enters or reclaims. Exact criteria for “reclaimed” vary and must be made explicit.

Open module →AdvancedPD Arrays

Suspension Block

A niche PD-array term appearing in secondary ICT transcript indexes. It is not consistently defined across accessible sources; the lesson treats it as a research term rather than a standard signal.

Open module →AdvancedPD Arrays

Vacuum Block

A niche label reported in secondary ICT transcript indexes for a price area associated with a fast move or limited trading through a region. The term is not consistently defined in the supplied playbook.

Open module →AdvancedTime & Session Concepts

New York Lunch Algorithmic Reversal (community label)

A community label for a possible midday reversal narrative. It is not a core model in the supplied playbook, which explicitly treats the NY lunch window (12:00–1:30 PM ET) as an avoid period.

Open module →AdvancedEntry Models

Market Maker Buy Model (MMBM)

A directional variant of the broader market-maker-model narrative, commonly described as a range/accumulation and possible sell-side manipulation followed by upside delivery. Exact phase boundaries vary.

Open module →AdvancedEntry Models

Market Maker Sell Model (MMSM)

A directional variant of the broader market-maker-model narrative, commonly described as range/accumulation and possible buy-side manipulation followed by downside delivery. Exact boundaries are discretionary.

Open module →AdvancedEntry Models

ICT 2022 Model

The supplied playbook describes this model as a liquidity raid followed by displacement with MSS, then a retracement into the FVG for execution. It is commonly associated with the 2022 Mentorship.

Open module →IntermediateEntry Models

Liquidity Sweep + MSS Model

A reversal framework that waits for a meaningful liquidity level to be swept, then requires a Market Structure Shift with displacement before considering a pullback entry.

Open module →IntermediateEntry Models

FVG Continuation Model

A continuation idea in which an impulsive move aligned with higher-timeframe context leaves an FVG and price later retraces into the imbalance before potentially continuing.

Open module →IntermediateEntry Models

Inversion FVG (IFVG) Reversal Model

The supplied playbook defines an IFVG when price body-closes through the far boundary of an existing FVG, changing its role. A retest entry is a further model convention.

Open module →AdvancedEntry Models

FVG + OTE Confluence Model

A confluence idea that looks for an FVG overlapping the 62%–79% retracement band of a defined impulse leg. The supplied playbook highlights 70.5% as a common reference.
